title: Selected-tab read omits smart chips
intent: Read the owner named in a native person chip.
bug: The selected-tab reader skips person, date and file chips, removing their visible names, dates and titles. Ordinary adjacent text and links survive. Plain gdoc cat and Workspace retain these chips. The illustrated name is anonymized.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.

before.label: BEFORE — NATIVE PERSON CHIP
before.diagnostic: Name anonymized: Alex Example represents the account owner.

expected.label: EXPECTED — READABLE CONTENT
expected.diagnostic: Retain the visible name; a hyperlink is also acceptable.

commands:
gdoc cat DOC --tab TAB --account PERSONAL
gdoc cat DOC --account PERSONAL
setup: Setup: create native chips with chips.py. Alex Example represents the account owner; no other person was contacted.

title: Windows TSV imports hidden carriage returns
intent: Import a two-column TSV file whose lines end with CRLF.
bug: The TSV reader removes LF but leaves CR in each final cell. The cells can look normal, but exact comparisons and header lookup fail. The same values with LF-only TSV or CRLF CSV import correctly.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.

expected.label: EXPECTED — GOOGLE SHEETS
expected.diagnostic: Stored B2: "100". Exact comparison with "100": TRUE.

observed.label: OBSERVED — GOOGLE SHEETS
observed.diagnostic: Stored B2: "100\r". Exact comparison: FALSE. The CR is invisible.

commands: gdoc cells SHEET Data!A1 --file crlf.tsv --account PERSONAL
setup: Setup: use literal CRLF line endings, not the displayed backslash escapes. The diagram normalizes the tested range to A1:B2.

title: Ten-digit identifier becomes list numbering
intent: Write the literal line identifying revenue account 1234567890.
bug: A line starting with a ten-digit number and a period is treated as a numbered list. The identifier disappears and Google renders item 1 instead. CommonMark limits ordered-list markers to nine digits; the independent parser treats this input as plain text.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.
commands:
gdoc cat DOC --tab TAB --account PERSONAL
gdoc write DOC specimen.md --tab TAB --account PERSONAL

title: Bracketed link label becomes literal Markdown
bug: A valid link label containing nested square brackets is not parsed as a link. The entire Markdown expression becomes visible prose. gdoc also emits this syntax when exporting a native link with that label, so its own output cannot make the round trip.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.
commands:
gdoc cat DOC --tab TAB --account PERSONAL
gdoc write DOC specimen.md --tab TAB --account PERSONAL

title: Entity text changes hyperlink parameters
intent: Create a Budget link whose query has parameters a=1 and b=2.
bug: The Markdown entity & is stored literally in the link destination. Its second query key becomes amp;b rather than b. The visible Budget label remains correct, so checking only document text misses the failure.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.
commands:
gdoc cat DOC --tab TAB --account PERSONAL
gdoc write DOC specimen.md --tab TAB --account PERSONAL

title: Merged label receives its neighbor’s edit
intent: Replace the visible cell immediately right of Merged A with Updated.
bug: Label-based cell selection moves one underlying column instead of past the merged span. It targets a covered slot; Google appends the replacement into the merged label, leaving the visible neighbor unchanged. Explicit column selection succeeds. A fresh three-column-span specimen reproduced the error.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.
commands: gdoc edit DOC Updated --cell "Merged A" --tab TAB --account PERSONAL
setup: Setup: import the one-row colspan=2 table from structure.py. The CLI documents --cell as replacing the cell to the right of the label; --col 2 is the passing control.

title: A phantom text match deletes the chip
intent: Replace the literal phrase "Before  after" with "Replacement".
bug: gdoc concatenates text on either side of a chip into a phrase that is not actually contiguous, then deletes the chip while replacing that phrase. Both person and file chips were lost. Google’s native replacement and Workspace find zero matches and preserve the chip. Adjacent ordinary edits pass.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.

before.label: BEFORE — NATIVE PERSON CHIP
before.diagnostic: Name anonymized. Selected-tab cat misleadingly reports: Before  after.

expected.diagnostic: Native Google and Workspace: 0 matches; chip preserved.

observed.diagnostic: gdoc reports 1 replacement; native person count drops from 1 to 0.

commands:
gdoc cat DOC --tab TAB --account PERSONAL
gdoc edit DOC "Before  after" Replacement --tab TAB --account PERSONAL
setup: Setup: use the person-chip paragraph from chips-edits.py; two spaces separate Before and after in the search phrase. Alex Example is an anonymized account name.

title: A literal Greek character cannot be found
intent: Replace the actual uppercase Σ in ΟΣ with X.
bug: Lowercasing the whole Greek word turns its final Σ into ς, while lowercasing the query Σ produces σ. gdoc then reports no match for the exact character present in the source. Google replaces it correctly. The same query in Budget Σ works in both tools.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.

before.label: BEFORE — NATIVE GOOGLE DOC
before.diagnostic: Find Σ (U+03A3); the source contains that exact character.

observed.diagnostic: gdoc exits 3: no match found. The document is unchanged.

commands: gdoc edit DOC "Σ" X --all --tab TAB --account PERSONAL
setup: Setup: insert the literal Greek characters ΟΣ into a blank native tab. The expected X is Latin; the initial Ο is Greek.
evidence_label: Fresh independent reproduction: gdoc exits 3; Google finds one match.

title: One comment becomes two malformed TSV records
intent: Read one multiline comment as stable TSV for another program.
bug: Comment text is interpolated into TSV without escaping or quoting embedded tabs and newlines. A quoting-aware TSV reader parses two records instead of one; Budget wrongly occupies the quote field. Native comment content and JSON output remain correct. Properly quoted multiline TSV is a passing control.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.

expected.data:
1 logical record; 5 fields
content: entire original comment
quote: empty
expected.label: EXPECTED — PARSED TSV RECORDS

observed.data:
Record 1: 5 fields
content: Question A; quote: Budget
Record 2: 2 fields
Is **100** final? Keep <5% and "quotes".
observed.label: OBSERVED — PARSED TSV RECORDS

commands:
gdoc comments DOC --plain --account PERSONAL
gdoc comments DOC --json --account PERSONAL
setup: Setup: create the single comment from review-commands.py. Parse stdout with csv.reader(delimiter="\t"); JSON is the passing control.
evidence_label: Live CLI stdout parsed independently; native comment data is intact.

title: UTF-8 file signature becomes part of the header
intent: Import a CSV whose UTF-8 encoding includes a byte-order signature.
bug: The importer treats the initial UTF-8 signature as a literal U+FEFF character in the first header. Item looks normal but no longer equals Item exactly. Native Google CSV import removes the signature and retains the intended header. This is an encoding interoperability defect, separate from CRLF handling.
novelty: Additional concrete regression trigger; broad campaign repair areas can overlap.

before.label: BEFORE — CSV FILE WITH UTF-8 SIGNATURE

expected.label: EXPECTED — GOOGLE SHEETS
expected.diagnostic: Stored A1: "Item". Character count: 4; exact match: TRUE.

observed.label: OBSERVED — GOOGLE SHEETS
observed.diagnostic: Stored A1 starts with invisible U+FEFF. Count: 5; exact match: FALSE.

commands: gdoc cells SHEET Data!A1 --file utf8-bom.csv --account PERSONAL
setup: Setup: write the CSV using UTF-8 with BOM (utf-8-sig). The diagram normalizes the tested range to A1:B2.
